2026-05-28.category: Types of Radioactive Decay, Except One
2026-05-28.explanation: Alpha, Beta, and Gamma are the three classic types of radioactive decay; Sigma denotes a sum or standard deviation in mathematics, not a form of radiation.

2026-05-29.category: Seven Summits, Except a Peak Left Off the List
2026-05-29.explanation: Everest, Aconcagua, and Denali are continental high points on the Seven Summits list; Mont Blanc is the Alps' highest peak, but Europe's official entry on that list is Mount Elbrus.

2026-05-30.category: Authors Who Wrote Under a Pen Name, Except One
2026-05-30.explanation: Mark Twain, George Orwell, and Lewis Carroll are pen names for Samuel Clemens, Eric Blair, and Charles Dodgson; Charles Dickens published under his own real name.

2026-05-31.category: Months Named After Latin Numbers, Except One
2026-05-31.explanation: September, October, and November come from the Latin words for seven, eight, and nine, reflecting their place in the old Roman calendar; August was renamed to honor Emperor Augustus.

2026-06-01.category: Michelangelo Sculptures, Except a Rodin Work
2026-06-01.explanation: David, the Pieta, and Moses were all sculpted by Michelangelo; The Thinker was sculpted by Auguste Rodin, centuries later.

2026-06-02.explanation: Locke, Hume, and Berkeley are the classic British Empiricist philosophers; Descartes founded Continental Rationalism, arguing from reason rather than sense experience.

2026-06-03.category: Fundamental Forces of Physics, Except One
2026-06-03.explanation: Gravity, Electromagnetism, and the Strong Nuclear Force are three of physics' four fundamental forces; Friction is an everyday force that emerges from electromagnetic interactions, not a fundamental one.

2026-06-04.explanation: Kingdom, Phylum, and Family are formal ranks in Linnaean taxonomy; Breed is an informal term for varieties within a domesticated species, not a taxonomic rank.

2026-06-05.category: Treaties That Ended Wars, Except One
2026-06-05.explanation: The Treaties of Versailles, Ghent, and Paris were all signed to end wars; the Treaty of Tordesillas divided newly claimed lands between Spain and Portugal, not a peace settlement.

2026-06-06.explanation: The Caspian Sea, Aral Sea, and Dead Sea are landlocked salt lakes despite their names; the Red Sea genuinely connects to the open ocean via the Gulf of Aden.

2026-06-07.category: Moons of Jupiter, Except a Moon of Saturn
2026-06-07.explanation: Europa, Io, and Ganymede are three of Jupiter's four Galilean moons; Titan is Saturn's largest moon.

2026-06-08.explanation: Diamond, Graphite, and Graphene are all pure forms of carbon; Quartz is a mineral made of silicon dioxide.

2026-06-09.explanation: Elizabeth I, Victoria, and Catherine the Great ruled as monarchs in their own right; Marie Antoinette was queen only by marriage to King Louis XVI of France.

2026-06-10.category: Lead Fictional Detectives, Except the Narrator
2026-06-10.explanation: Sherlock Holmes, Hercule Poirot, and Miss Marple are the detectives who solve their stories' central mysteries; Dr. Watson is Holmes's companion and chronicler, not the lead investigator.

2026-06-11.explanation: Vatican City, Monaco, and Singapore are true city-states, each a single urban area forming the whole country; Luxembourg is small but has multiple cities and open countryside.

2026-06-12.category: Zodiac Constellations, Except a Famous Non-Member
2026-06-12.explanation: Leo, Scorpius, and Aquarius all lie along the zodiac band the sun appears to cross; Orion is one of the sky's most recognizable constellations, but it isn't a zodiac constellation.

2026-06-13.category: Cricket Match Formats, Except a Tennis Term
2026-06-13.explanation: Test Match, One Day International, and T20 are formats of international cricket; Grand Slam is a term from tennis and golf.

2026-06-14.explanation: Vinegar, Lemon Juice, and Battery Acid are all acidic, with pH well below 7; Baking Soda is alkaline, with a pH around 9.

2026-06-15.category: ABO Blood Types, Except a Different System
2026-06-15.explanation: Type A, Type B, and Type AB are ABO blood types; the Rh Factor is a separate antigen system layered on top, giving each ABO type its positive or negative label.

2026-06-16.explanation: Waterloo, Trafalgar, and Austerlitz were all fought during the Napoleonic Wars in the early 1800s; Agincourt was fought four centuries earlier, during the Hundred Years' War.

2026-06-17.explanation: Circle, Ellipse, and Parabola are conic sections formed by slicing a cone; a Rhombus is a four-sided polygon, not a conic section.

2026-06-18.explanation: Kangaroo, Koala, and Wombat are marsupials that carry their young in a pouch; the Platypus is a monotreme, a mammal that lays eggs.

2026-06-19.category: Baroque Composers, Except a Classical-Era Figure
2026-06-19.explanation: Bach, Handel, and Vivaldi were leading composers of the Baroque era; Haydn belongs to the later Classical era and is often called the father of the symphony.

2026-06-20.category: Elements With No Stable Isotopes, Except a Common Stable One
2026-06-20.explanation: Technetium, Promethium, and Francium have no stable isotopes and are always radioactive; Copper is common and stable.

2026-06-21.category: Shakespeare Plays Set in Italy vs Play Set in Denmark
2026-06-21.explanation: Romeo and Juliet (Verona), Othello (Venice and Cyprus), and The Merchant of Venice (Venice) are set in Italy; Hamlet is set in Denmark.

2026-06-22.category: Verbs With Identical Present and Past Tense vs a Regular Verb
2026-06-22.explanation: Put, Cut, and Hit are unchanged in the past tense; Walk becomes 'walked,' changing form.

2026-06-23.category: Countries Where English Is Official but Not Dominant vs Native English-Speaking Country
2026-06-23.explanation: Nigeria, India, and the Philippines list English as an official language though it is not most residents' first language; in Australia, English is the dominant native language.

2026-06-24.category: Chess Pieces That Cannot Jump vs the Knight
2026-06-24.explanation: The Bishop, Rook, and Queen must move along a clear, unobstructed line; the Knight is the only piece that can jump over other pieces.

2026-06-25.category: Nations Widely Cited as Never Colonized vs a Colonized Nation
2026-06-25.explanation: Ethiopia, Thailand, and Nepal are widely cited as nations that avoided formal European colonization; Vietnam was colonized by France as part of French Indochina.

2026-06-26.category: Anagrams of Each Other vs a Look-Alike Word
2026-06-26.explanation: Listen, Silent, and Enlist are all anagrams of each other, sharing the same six letters; Silence has an extra letter and is not an anagram of the other three.

2026-06-27.category: SI Base Units vs Derived Unit
2026-06-27.explanation: Kilogram, Meter, and Second are SI base units; the Newton, a unit of force, is a derived unit defined in terms of the base units.

2026-06-28.category: Treaties Ending World War I vs a World War II Treaty
2026-06-28.explanation: The Treaties of Versailles, Saint-Germain, and Trianon concluded World War I for Germany, Austria, and Hungary respectively; the Treaty of San Francisco formally ended the state of war between the Allies and Japan in 1951.

2026-06-29.category: Words That Shift Meaning Entirely When Pluralized, Except One That Doesn't
2026-06-29.explanation: Glass, Custom, and Arm take on entirely different meanings in their plural forms ("glasses" = eyewear, "customs" = border control, "arms" = weapons); "Books" simply means more than one book, with no shift in meaning.

2026-06-30.category: Authors' Pen Names vs an Author's Real Name
2026-06-30.explanation: George Orwell, Mark Twain, and Lewis Carroll are pen names for Eric Blair, Samuel Clemens, and Charles Dodgson; Jane Austen published under her own real name.

2026-07-01.category: Rivers That Reach the Ocean vs a River Ending in an Inland Sea
2026-07-01.explanation: The Amazon, Nile, and Mississippi all empty into the ocean or a sea connected to it; the Volga empties into the landlocked Caspian Sea, which has no natural outlet to the ocean.

2026-07-02.explanation: Orion, Cassiopeia, and Ursa Major are constellations; Sirius is a single star, the brightest in the night sky, not a constellation.

2026-07-03.category: Homophones of Each Other vs a Non-Matching Number Word
2026-07-03.explanation: To, Too, and Two are all pronounced identically; Three has a distinct pronunciation and doesn't share the sound.

2026-07-04.category: Roman Emperors vs a Roman Republican Statesman
2026-07-04.explanation: Augustus, Nero, and Caligula were Roman emperors; Cicero was a statesman and orator of the earlier Roman Republic who died before the Empire began and never held imperial power.

2026-07-05.category: Landlocked African Countries vs a Coastal African Country
2026-07-05.explanation: Chad, Mali, and Niger are landlocked African nations; Nigeria has a coastline on the Gulf of Guinea.

2026-07-06.explanation: The Electron, Muon, and Tau are all leptons; the Quark belongs to a different family of fundamental particles.

2026-07-07.category: Fictional Detectives vs a Real Historical Detective
2026-07-07.explanation: Sherlock Holmes, Hercule Poirot, and Miss Marple are fictional detectives from literature; Allan Pinkerton was a real 19th-century detective who founded the Pinkerton Detective Agency.

2026-07-08.category: Alkali Metals vs an Alkaline Earth Metal
2026-07-08.explanation: Sodium, Potassium, and Lithium are alkali metals in Group 1; Calcium is an alkaline earth metal in Group 2.

2026-07-09.category: Bill of Rights Amendments vs a Later Amendment
2026-07-09.explanation: The First, Second, and Fourth Amendments are part of the original 1791 Bill of Rights; the Nineteenth Amendment, granting women's suffrage, was ratified in 1920.

2026-07-10.explanation: Racecar, Level, and Rotator all read the same forwards and backwards; Camera does not.

2026-07-11.category: Countries Entirely in the Southern Hemisphere vs a Country That Straddles the Equator
2026-07-11.explanation: New Zealand, Uruguay, and Paraguay lie entirely within the Southern Hemisphere; Brazil's territory extends across the equator into the Northern Hemisphere too.

2026-07-12.category: Standard String Quartet Instruments vs a Non-Quartet String Instrument
2026-07-12.explanation: Violin, Viola, and Cello make up the standard string quartet; the Double Bass is not included, joining instead to form a string quintet.

2026-07-13.category: Assassinated US Presidents vs a President Who Survived an Attempt
2026-07-13.explanation: Lincoln, Garfield, and McKinley were all assassinated while in office; Reagan survived an assassination attempt in 1981.

2026-07-14.category: Contronyms (Words That Are Their Own Opposite) vs a Regular Word
2026-07-14.explanation: Cleave (to split or to join), Sanction (to permit or to penalize), and Dust (to add fine particles or to remove them) are contronyms with opposite meanings; Big has only one meaning.

2026-07-15.category: Types of Chemical Bonds vs an Atomic Variant Term
2026-07-15.explanation: Ionic, Covalent, and Hydrogen bonds are all types of chemical bonding; an Isotope refers to atoms of an element with differing neutron counts, not a bond type.

2026-07-16.category: Types of Teeth vs the Substance Coating Them
2026-07-16.explanation: Incisors, Canines, and Molars are types of teeth; Enamel is the hard substance that coats teeth, not a type of tooth.

2026-07-17.category: Perfect Squares vs a Perfect Cube
2026-07-17.explanation: Sixteen (4 squared), Thirty-Six (6 squared), and Forty-Nine (7 squared) are perfect squares; Twenty-Seven is a perfect cube (3 cubed), not a perfect square.

2026-07-18.category: Novels Narrated in First Person vs a Third-Person Novel
2026-07-18.explanation: Moby-Dick, The Great Gatsby, and Jane Eyre are all told by first-person narrators; Pride and Prejudice is narrated in the third person.

2026-07-19.category: Metric Prefixes for Fractions vs a Multiple Prefix
2026-07-19.explanation: Milli-, Micro-, and Nano- represent fractions smaller than one; Kilo- represents a multiple, one thousand times larger than the base unit.

2026-07-20.category: Cold War Proxy Conflicts vs a Pre-Cold War War
2026-07-20.explanation: The Korean War, Vietnam War, and Soviet-Afghan War were Cold War-era proxy conflicts; World War II ended in 1945, before the Cold War began.

2026-07-21.category: The Lord of the Rings Trilogy vs Its Prequel Novel
2026-07-21.explanation: The Fellowship of the Ring, The Two Towers, and The Return of the King form the Lord of the Rings trilogy; The Hobbit is Tolkien's earlier, standalone prequel novel.

2026-07-22.category: Galaxy Shape Classifications vs a Nebula
2026-07-22.explanation: Spiral, Elliptical, and Irregular are classifications of galaxy shapes; a Nebula is a cloud of gas and dust, not a galaxy.

2026-07-23.category: Former Ottoman Territories vs a Country Never Ruled by the Ottomans
2026-07-23.explanation: Greece, Serbia, and Egypt were all once territories of the Ottoman Empire; Portugal was never under Ottoman rule.

2026-07-24.category: Men's Golf Majors vs a Non-Major Tournament
2026-07-24.explanation: The Masters, The Open Championship, and the PGA Championship are three of golf's four major championships (along with the US Open); The Players Championship is prestigious but not officially a major.

2026-07-25.category: Types of Chemical Reactions vs a Reaction-Speeding Substance
2026-07-25.explanation: Synthesis, Decomposition, and Combustion are types of chemical reactions; a Catalyst is a substance that speeds up a reaction without being a reaction type itself.

2026-07-26.category: Post-Soviet Countries vs a Post-Yugoslav Country
2026-07-26.explanation: Ukraine, Kazakhstan, and Belarus became independent nations after the 1991 dissolution of the Soviet Union; Croatia became independent that same year, but from the breakup of Yugoslavia, not the USSR.

2026-07-27.category: Music Release Formats, Except a Written Document
2026-07-27.explanation: Album, Single, and EP are all formats for releasing recorded music; a Manuscript is a handwritten or typed document, not a music release.

2026-07-28.category: Noble Gases, Except a Diatomic Gas
2026-07-28.explanation: Neon, Argon, and Krypton are monatomic noble gases; Hydrogen naturally exists as a two-atom molecule, H2.

2026-07-29.explanation: Oxygen's symbol O matches its English name, while Lead (Pb), Tin (Sn), and Potassium (K) get their symbols from Latin names (Plumbum, Stannum, Kalium).

2026-07-30.explanation: Nepal's flag is the only national flag in the world that isn't a rectangle, formed instead from two stacked triangular pennants, while Switzerland, Vatican City, and Japan all fly rectangular or square flags.

2026-07-31.explanation: Sonar reads differently backward (ranos), so it isn't a palindrome, while Level, Radar, and Rotor all read the same forward and backward.

2026-08-01.explanation: Canada's flag features a red maple leaf, while Sweden, Brazil, and Argentina all have flags with no red in them at all.

2026-08-02.explanation: Ethiopia successfully resisted European colonization (aside from a brief WWII-era Italian occupation), while Kenya, Nigeria, and Ghana were all formally colonized by European powers.

2026-08-03.explanation: Safari traces back to Swahili and Arabic, while Tycoon, Tsunami, and Karaoke all entered English from Japanese.

2026-08-04.category: A Day Shorter Than a Year
2026-08-04.explanation: Venus's rotation takes about 243 Earth days, longer than its 225-day orbit around the Sun, while Earth, Mars, and Jupiter all have a day far shorter than their year.

2026-08-05.explanation: Insult contains a U instead of an E, so its letters don't rearrange into Listen, while Silent, Enlist, and Tinsel are all true anagrams of it.

2026-08-06.category: SI Units Named for Electrical Pioneers, Except a Unit of Energy
2026-08-06.explanation: Ampere, Volt, and Ohm all measure electrical properties (current, potential, resistance); the Joule measures energy, not specifically electricity.

2026-08-07.explanation: Wimbledon is the only Grand Slam still played on grass, while the US Open, Australian Open, and French Open are played on hard court or clay.

2026-08-08.explanation: Bromine is the only nonmetal that is liquid at room temperature, while Chlorine and Fluorine are gases and Iodine is a solid.

2026-08-09.explanation: Boston has never served as the capital of the United States, while Philadelphia, New York City, and Annapolis each did at different points.

2026-08-10.explanation: Albert Einstein won only a single Nobel Prize (Physics, 1921), while Marie Curie, Linus Pauling, and John Bardeen each won two.

2026-08-11.explanation: Nylon is a coined trademark name with no place origin, while Denim (Nîmes), Cashmere (Kashmir), and Jeans (Genoa) are all named after real places.

2026-08-12.explanation: Lake Winnipeg is a separate Canadian lake, not one of the five Great Lakes, while Huron, Ontario, and Erie all are.

words: Down and Out in Paris and London
2026-08-13.explanation: Brave New World was written by Aldous Huxley, while Animal Farm, Nineteen Eighty-Four, and Down and Out in Paris and London are all by George Orwell.

2026-08-14.explanation: The Red Panda is a placental mammal from the Himalayas, not a marsupial, while Koala, Wombat, and Tasmanian Devil are all Australian marsupials.

2026-08-15.explanation: Amethyst is simply a purple variety of quartz, not its own official reference mineral, while Talc, Gypsum, and Quartz are three of the ten standard Mohs scale minerals.

2026-08-16.category: Moons of Jupiter, Except a Moon of Mars
2026-08-16.explanation: Europa, Ganymede, and Callisto are all moons of Jupiter; Phobos orbits Mars.

2026-08-17.explanation: Sudoku is a Japanese term meaning 'single number,' not derived from a person, while Sandwich, Cardigan, and Boycott are all named after real people.

2026-08-18.explanation: West Germany did not join NATO until 1955, while the United States, United Kingdom, and France were founding members in 1949.

2026-08-19.explanation: Nitrogen makes up most of Earth's atmosphere but isn't a significant greenhouse gas, while Carbon Dioxide, Methane, and Nitrous Oxide all trap heat.

2026-08-20.category: National Anthems With No Official Lyrics, Except One With Sung Lyrics
2026-08-20.explanation: Spain, San Marino, and Kosovo all have national anthems with no official lyrics; France's anthem, "La Marseillaise," has well-known sung lyrics.

2026-08-21.category: Influential Figures Who Never Won a Nobel Prize, Except One Who Did
2026-08-21.explanation: Gandhi, Tolstoy, and Freud are all famously overlooked by the Nobel committee; Marie Curie won the Nobel Prize twice, in Physics and Chemistry.

2026-08-22.explanation: The Coral Sea lies near Australia in the Pacific, nowhere near Europe, while the Mediterranean, Baltic, and North Seas all border European coastlines.

2026-08-23.explanation: Umbrella has no animal name hidden in its spelling, while Scatter hides CAT, Cowardly hides COW, and Ratchet hides RAT.

2026-08-24.explanation: Ulysses S. Grant survived his presidency and died years later, while Lincoln, Garfield, and McKinley were all assassinated while in office.

2026-08-25.explanation: Eighteen does not appear in the Fibonacci sequence, while Eight, Thirteen, and Twenty-One all do.

2026-08-26.explanation: Andromeda, Orion, and Cassiopeia are constellations; Vega is a single star, one of the brightest in the night sky, located in the constellation Lyra.

2026-08-27.explanation: The Liter is not named after a person, while the Watt, Kelvin, and Pascal are all eponymous units honoring scientists.

2026-08-28.explanation: Senegal has an Atlantic coastline, while Chad, Niger, and Mali are all landlocked.

2026-08-29.category: Axial Tilt of the Gas Giants
2026-08-29.explanation: Uranus has an extreme tilt of nearly 98 degrees and essentially spins on its side, while Saturn, Neptune, and Jupiter all have much more modest tilts.

2026-08-30.explanation: South Africa had already been a self-governing dominion since 1910 and wasn't part of the 1960 independence wave, while Nigeria, Somalia, and Madagascar all gained independence that year.

2026-08-31.category: Contronyms (Words That Are Their Own Opposite)
2026-08-31.explanation: Enormous simply means very large with no opposite sense, while Cleave, Sanction, and Dust can each mean two contradictory things.

2026-09-01.explanation: A Platelet is a cell fragment involved in clotting, not a white blood cell, while Neutrophil, Lymphocyte, and Monocyte are all types of white blood cells.

2026-09-02.explanation: Mozart died at 35 with no record of hearing loss, while Beethoven, Smetana, and Fauré each experienced significant deafness later in life.

2026-09-03.explanation: Nevada does not touch the Mexican border, while Texas, New Mexico, and Arizona all do.

2026-09-04.explanation: Jefferson was a statesman and diplomat, never a general, while Washington, Eisenhower, and Grant all commanded armies before becoming president.

2026-09-05.category: Words That Spell a New Word Backward
2026-09-05.explanation: Music spells the nonsense string 'cisum' in reverse, while Stressed becomes Desserts, Diaper becomes Repaid, and Drawer becomes Reward when reversed.

2026-09-06.category: Constructed Fictional Languages, Except a Real Constructed Language
2026-09-06.explanation: Klingon, Dothraki, and Na'vi were invented for the Star Trek, Game of Thrones, and Avatar franchises; Esperanto is a real-world constructed language designed for international communication, not fiction.

2026-09-07.category: Spanish-Speaking South American Countries, Except a Dutch-Speaking One
2026-09-07.explanation: Argentina, Uruguay, and Paraguay are all Spanish-speaking; Suriname's official language is Dutch.

2026-09-08.explanation: "Novel" is not a palindrome; "Civic," "Kayak," and "Rotor" all read the same forwards and backwards.

2026-09-09.category: Silent-Letter Words vs Fully Pronounced Word
2026-09-09.explanation: Every letter in "Sunset" is pronounced; "Knight," "Comb," and "Wrist" each contain a silent letter (the K/GH, the B, and the W).

2026-09-10.category: Africa's Big Five vs Non-Big-Five Animal
2026-09-10.explanation: The cheetah is not one of Africa's traditional "Big Five" game animals; Leopard, Buffalo, and Rhino are three of the Big Five, along with lion and elephant.

2026-09-11.explanation: F Major's key signature has one flat (B-flat); G Major, D Major, and A Major key signatures consist entirely of sharps.

2026-09-12.category: Capital Equals Largest City vs Not
2026-09-12.explanation: Albany is New York's capital, but New York City is the state's largest city; Phoenix, Boston, and Denver are each both the capital and the largest city of their respective states.

2026-09-13.explanation: "Aquarium" derives from Latin ("aqua," water); "Democracy," "Telephone," and "Philosophy" all derive from Greek roots.

2026-09-14.explanation: English is written left-to-right; Arabic, Hebrew, and Urdu are all written right-to-left.

2026-09-15.explanation: Macbeth, Othello, and King Lear are among Shakespeare's great tragedies; As You Like It is one of his comedies.

2026-09-16.category: SI Derived Units, Except a Base Unit
2026-09-16.explanation: Pascal (pressure), Watt (power), and Joule (energy) are all SI derived units; the Second is one of the seven SI base units.

2026-09-17.explanation: Julius Caesar was a dictator of the Roman Republic and never held the official title of emperor; Augustus, Nero, and Trajan were all official Roman emperors.

2026-09-18.explanation: Neon exists as single, uncombined atoms; Oxygen, Nitrogen, and Hydrogen naturally occur as diatomic molecules (O2, N2, H2).

2026-09-19.explanation: Poland lies entirely within Europe; Turkey, Russia, and Egypt each have territory spanning two continents.

2026-09-20.category: 19th-Century British Novelists, Except a Russian Novelist
2026-09-20.explanation: Thomas Hardy, George Eliot, and Jane Austen were all British novelists of the 19th century; Leo Tolstoy was Russian.

2026-09-21.category: Equator-Crossing Countries vs Nearby Non-Crossing Country
2026-09-21.explanation: The equator does not pass through Peru, which lies entirely to its south; Ecuador, Kenya, and Indonesia are all crossed by the equator.

2026-09-22.explanation: Seventy-two is not a perfect square; Sixty-four (8 squared), Eighty-one (9 squared), and Forty-nine (7 squared) are all perfect squares.

2026-09-23.category: Actors Who Played James Bond vs Actor Who Never Did
2026-09-23.explanation: Liam Neeson has never played James Bond; Sean Connery, Roger Moore, and Daniel Craig have all portrayed 007 in the film franchise.

2026-09-24.explanation: Sodium is a highly reactive alkali metal that reacts violently with water; Gold, Platinum, and Silver are noble metals prized for their resistance to corrosion.

2026-09-25.category: Never-Colonized Nations vs Formerly Colonized Nation
2026-09-25.explanation: India was colonized by the British Empire; Ethiopia, Thailand, and Nepal are among the few nations never formally colonized by a European power.

2026-09-26.explanation: Iodine is a solid at room temperature that sublimes into a purple vapor when heated; Fluorine, Helium, and Chlorine are all gases at room temperature.

2026-09-27.explanation: The Bill of Rights (the first ten amendments) was ratified in 1791, in the 18th century; the 19th, 21st, and 18th Amendments were all ratified in the 20th century.

2026-09-28.category: Same Singular/Plural Words vs Regular Plural
2026-09-28.explanation: "Cats" takes a regular plural ending in -s; "Sheep," "Deer," and "Moose" are all words whose singular and plural forms are identical.

2026-09-29.category: US Presidents Who Won the Nobel Peace Prize, Except One Who Didn't
2026-09-29.explanation: Theodore Roosevelt, Woodrow Wilson, and Barack Obama each won the Nobel Peace Prize; Franklin D. Roosevelt never received the award, despite leading the US through WWII.

2026-09-30.explanation: Japan has a single capital, Tokyo; South Africa, Bolivia, and Sri Lanka are among the handful of countries that officially designate more than one capital city.

2026-10-01.category: Elements With No Stable Isotopes vs a Stable Element
2026-10-01.explanation: Iron has several stable, non-radioactive isotopes; Technetium, Promethium, and Uranium have no stable isotopes at all, meaning every form of these elements is radioactive.

2026-10-02.category: Southern African Countries, Except an East African One
2026-10-02.explanation: Namibia, Botswana, and Zimbabwe are all in Southern Africa; Kenya is in East Africa.

2026-10-03.category: Alkali Metals vs Alkaline Earth Metal
2026-10-03.explanation: Magnesium is an alkaline earth metal (Group 2); Potassium, Sodium, and Lithium are alkali metals (Group 1).

2026-10-04.explanation: Harry Truman never served as a general, holding the rank of captain in the Army; Washington, Grant, and Eisenhower each held the rank of general before becoming president.

2026-10-05.category: Country Names That Double as English Words vs One That Doesn't
2026-10-05.explanation: "Angola" is not a common English word or given name outside of the country itself; "Turkey," "Chad," and "Jordan" are country names that double as an everyday English word or common first name.

2026-10-06.category: Muscle Tissue Types vs Nerve Cell
2026-10-06.explanation: A neuron is a nerve cell, not a muscle tissue; Cardiac, Smooth, and Skeletal are the three types of muscle tissue in the human body.

2026-10-07.category: Rivers That Flow North vs a South-Flowing River
2026-10-07.explanation: The Mississippi River flows south into the Gulf of Mexico; the Nile, Ob, and Mackenzie are major rivers that flow north.

2026-10-08.category: String Quartet Instruments vs Wind Instrument
2026-10-08.explanation: The oboe is a woodwind instrument; a standard string quartet consists of two Violins, a Viola, and a Cello.

2026-10-09.explanation: Stratus clouds form at low altitude; Cirrus, Cirrostratus, and Cirrocumulus are all high-altitude clouds, named with the "cirro-" prefix.

2026-10-10.category: Prime Numbers, Except a Composite Number
2026-10-10.explanation: Twenty-Nine, Thirty-One, and Thirty-Seven are all prime; Thirty-Three equals 3 x 11, making it composite.

2026-10-11.category: WWII Allied Powers vs Axis Power
2026-10-11.explanation: Italy fought as one of the three main Axis powers, alongside Germany and Japan, for most of World War II; the United Kingdom, Soviet Union, and United States were all major Allied powers.

2026-10-12.category: Irregular Greek Plurals vs Regular -S Plural
2026-10-12.explanation: "Album" simply adds -s to form its plural ("albums"); "Analysis," "Crisis," and "Thesis" all take irregular Greek-derived plurals ending in -es ("analyses," "crises," "theses").

2026-10-13.category: Island Nations With No Other Country on Their Island, Except One That Shares It
2026-10-13.explanation: Iceland, Japan, and Sri Lanka each occupy their entire island landmass with no other country present; Haiti shares the island of Hispaniola with the Dominican Republic.

2026-10-14.explanation: Voltage is a variable physical quantity that changes depending on the circuit; the Speed of Light, Planck's Constant, and Avogadro's Number are fixed physical constants.

2026-10-15.category: Commonwealth Realms With the British Monarch as Head of State, Except a Republic
2026-10-15.explanation: Australia, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom all recognize the British monarch as head of state; Ireland is an independent republic with its own president.

2026-10-16.category: US State Names From Native American Words, Except One Named for a Monarch
2026-10-16.explanation: Ohio, Michigan, and Dakota all derive their names from Native American words; Georgia was named in honor of Britain's King George II.

2026-10-17.category: Countries With Only One Land Border vs. One With Several
2026-10-17.explanation: Portugal, South Korea, and Qatar each share a border with only one other country, while Turkey borders eight countries.

2026-10-18.category: Words That Are Their Own Plural vs. One That Changes
2026-10-18.explanation: Sheep, Deer, and Moose stay the same in the plural, while Goose becomes 'geese.'

2026-10-19.category: Europe's Smallest Microstates, Except a Full-Sized Country
2026-10-19.explanation: Monaco, Vatican City, and San Marino are among Europe's smallest microstates; the Netherlands is a full-sized country.

2026-10-20.category: Noble Gases, Except a Liquid Metal
2026-10-20.explanation: Radon, Xenon, and Krypton are noble gases; Mercury is a metal that's liquid at room temperature.

2026-10-21.category: Members of NATO's Eastern Flank Since the 1990s-2000s, Except a Non-Member
2026-10-21.explanation: Czechia, Slovakia, and Hungary all joined NATO by 2004; Ukraine is not a NATO member.

2026-10-22.category: Shakespeare Plays With a Ghost vs. One Without
2026-10-22.explanation: Hamlet, Macbeth, and Julius Caesar all feature a ghost central to the plot, while Twelfth Night has no ghost at all.

2026-10-23.category: Tempo Markings vs. a Dynamic Marking
2026-10-23.explanation: Allegro, Andante, and Presto are all musical tempo markings telling you how fast to play, while Forte is a dynamic marking telling you how loud.

2026-10-24.category: Noble Gases, Except a Reactive Halogen
2026-10-24.explanation: Argon, Xenon, and Radon are noble gases; Fluorine is the most reactive halogen on the periodic table.

2026-10-25.category: Beatles Songs Credited to Lennon-McCartney vs. a George Harrison Song
2026-10-25.explanation: Yesterday, Let It Be, and Hey Jude were all officially credited to Lennon-McCartney, while Something was written solely by George Harrison.

2026-10-26.category: Cities That Hosted the Olympics Multiple Times vs. One That Hosted Once
2026-10-26.explanation: London, Paris, and Los Angeles have each hosted the Summer Olympics more than once, while Rio de Janeiro hosted only in 2016.

2026-10-27.category: Island Nations, Except a Landlocked Country
2026-10-27.explanation: Taiwan, the Philippines, and Sri Lanka are all islands; Switzerland is landlocked in the middle of Europe.

2026-10-28.category: Noble Gases, Except a Compound Gas
2026-10-28.explanation: Argon, Neon, and Xenon are noble gases, each a single element; Carbon Dioxide is a compound made of carbon and oxygen.

2026-10-29.category: Words From Sanskrit or Hindi vs. a Word From Inuktitut
2026-10-29.explanation: Jungle, Bungalow, and Shampoo all trace back to Sanskrit or Hindi, while Igloo comes from the Inuktitut word for house.

2026-10-30.category: Thomas Edison Inventions vs. Alexander Graham Bell's Invention
2026-10-30.explanation: The Phonograph, Motion Picture Camera, and Nickel-Iron Battery were all invented by Thomas Edison; the Telephone was patented by Alexander Graham Bell.

2026-10-31.category: Southeast Asian Countries, Except an East Asian One
2026-10-31.explanation: Laos, Cambodia, and Thailand are all in Southeast Asia; Mongolia is in East Asia.

2026-11-01.category: Countries Named After a Person, Except One Named for a Geographic Feature
2026-11-01.explanation: Colombia, Bolivia, and Saudi Arabia are all named after people (Columbus, Simon Bolivar, and the House of Saud); Ecuador is named after the equator, which runs through the country.

2026-11-02.category: Connected Bones vs. the One Bone That Isn't
2026-11-02.explanation: The Femur, Tibia, and Humerus all form joints with neighboring bones, while the Hyoid, in the throat, is the only bone in the body not connected to another.

2026-11-03.category: Portuguese-Speaking Countries vs. a Spanish-Speaking Country
2026-11-03.explanation: Brazil, Angola, and Mozambique are all officially Portuguese-speaking nations, while Argentina's official language is Spanish.

2026-11-04.category: Currencies Named After a Person vs. One Named for the Sun
2026-11-04.explanation: The Bolivar, Balboa, and Lempira are all named after historical figures, while Peru's Sol takes its name from the Spanish word for sun.

2026-11-05.category: Flags With No Red vs. One That Has Red
2026-11-05.explanation: The flags of Ireland, Jamaica, and Brazil contain no red at all, while Mexico's flag features a red stripe.

2026-11-06.category: Words With Silent Letters vs. One Without
2026-11-06.explanation: Knight, Gnome, and Debt all contain a silent letter, while every letter in Frost is pronounced.

2026-11-07.category: AKC Herding Group Breeds vs. a Sporting Group Breed
2026-11-07.explanation: The Border Collie, Australian Shepherd, and Corgi are all classified in the AKC's Herding Group, while the Labrador belongs to the Sporting Group.

2026-11-08.category: US Coins Featuring a President vs. One Featuring a Guide
2026-11-08.explanation: The Penny, Nickel, and Dime feature Lincoln, Jefferson, and Franklin D. Roosevelt, while the Sacagawea Dollar features Sacagawea, not a president.

2026-11-09.category: Words From Native American Languages vs. a Word of Old English Origin
2026-11-09.explanation: Moose, Raccoon, and Skunk all entered English from Native American languages, while Beaver comes from Old English.

2026-11-10.category: Caspian Sea Border Countries vs. a Landlocked Neighbor
2026-11-10.explanation: Russia, Iran, and Kazakhstan all border the Caspian Sea, while Uzbekistan, though nearby, is landlocked and does not touch it.

2026-11-11.category: Henry VIII's Wives Who Weren't Beheaded vs. One Who Was
2026-11-11.explanation: Catherine of Aragon, Jane Seymour, and Catherine Parr all avoided execution, while Anne Boleyn was beheaded in 1536.

2026-11-12.category: Great Lakes vs. a Lake That Isn't One of the Five
2026-11-12.explanation: Superior, Michigan, and Erie are three of the five Great Lakes, while Lake Champlain, on the US-Canada border, is not one of them.

2026-11-13.category: OPEC Members vs. a Major Non-OPEC Producer
2026-11-13.explanation: Saudi Arabia, Iran, and Venezuela are all members of OPEC, while Norway, despite major oil production, has never joined.

2026-11-14.category: Noble Gases, Except a Reactive Compound
2026-11-14.explanation: Xenon, Krypton, and Argon are noble gases, each a single element; Ozone (O3) is a reactive compound made of three oxygen atoms.

2026-11-15.category: Composers vs. the One Famous for Going Deaf
2026-11-15.explanation: Mozart, Brahms, and Handel are not remembered for hearing loss, while Beethoven famously composed his late masterpieces after going deaf.

2026-11-16.explanation: Krypton, Xenon, and Argon are all noble gases, while Chlorine belongs to the halogen group.

2026-11-17.category: Currencies of the Scandinavian Monetary Union vs. Finland's Old Currency
2026-11-17.explanation: The Danish Krone, Swedish Krona, and Norwegian Krone all originated in the 1873 Scandinavian Monetary Union, while Finland, then part of Russia, used the Markka outside it.

2026-11-18.category: Mediterranean Islands vs. an Indian Ocean Island
2026-11-18.explanation: Sicily, Corsica, and Crete are all islands in the Mediterranean Sea, while Zanzibar lies in the Indian Ocean off Tanzania.

2026-11-19.category: Metric Units, Except an Imperial Unit
2026-11-19.explanation: Liter, Gram, and Ampere all belong to the metric system; the Foot is a unit of the imperial system.

2026-11-20.category: African Deserts vs. a South American Desert
2026-11-20.explanation: The Sahara, Kalahari, and Namib deserts are all in Africa, while the Atacama Desert lies in Chile, South America.

2026-11-21.category: UN Security Council Permanent Members vs. a Country That Isn't
2026-11-21.explanation: The United States, Russia, and China are three of the five permanent UN Security Council members, while Germany holds no permanent seat.

2026-11-22.category: Rome's Five Good Emperors vs. an Infamous Tyrant
2026-11-22.explanation: Trajan, Hadrian, and Marcus Aurelius were three of Rome's 'Five Good Emperors,' while Caligula is remembered as a notorious tyrant.

2026-11-23.category: Metals That Melt Near Room Temperature, Solid Far Beyond It
2026-11-23.explanation: Tungsten has the highest melting point of any metal and stays solid far beyond room temperature; gallium, cesium, and rubidium are all metals that melt at or just above room temperature.

2026-11-24.category: Countries With One Land Neighbor, Borders the Most Nations
2026-11-24.explanation: Russia shares land borders with fourteen different countries, more than any other nation; Portugal, South Korea, and Haiti each border exactly one neighboring country.

2026-11-25.category: Units Named After Scientists, Not Named for a Person
2026-11-25.explanation: The kilogram is defined by a fundamental physical constant rather than named after a person; the newton, watt, and joule are all SI units named after the scientists Newton, Watt, and Joule.

2026-11-26.category: Rare Earth Elements, A Transition Metal
2026-11-26.explanation: Titanium is a transition metal, not a rare earth element; neodymium, europium, and yttrium are all classified as rare earth elements.

2026-11-27.category: Seven Sisters Colleges, Except a Non-Member Women's College
2026-11-27.explanation: Smith, Vassar, and Wellesley are three of the historic Seven Sisters colleges; Scripps College, though also a women's college, was founded later and is part of the Claremont Colleges, not the Seven Sisters.

2026-11-28.category: Olympic Ball Sports, No Ball Involved
2026-11-28.explanation: Fencing is contested with swords and involves no ball; water polo, handball, and rugby sevens are all Olympic sports played with a ball.

2026-11-29.category: Two-Time Nobel Laureates, Won Only One
2026-11-29.explanation: Einstein won a single Nobel Prize, in Physics in 1921; Marie Curie, Linus Pauling, and John Bardeen are each among the small handful of people who have won two Nobel Prizes.

2026-11-30.category: Same in Singular and Plural, A Regular Plural
2026-11-30.explanation: "Goats" takes a normal plural ending in -s; sheep, deer, and moose all keep the identical form whether singular or plural.

2026-12-01.category: Words With Silent First Letters, First Letter Pronounced
2026-12-01.explanation: The C in "castle" is pronounced normally; the K in "knight," the G in "gnome," and the P in "pterodactyl" are all silent.

2026-12-02.category: Symbols From Latin Names, Symbol Matches the English Name
2026-12-02.explanation: Nickel's symbol, Ni, is drawn directly from its English name; gold (Au), iron (Fe), and silver (Ag) all have symbols derived from their Latin names instead.

2026-12-03.category: High-Altitude Clouds, Forms at Low Altitude
2026-12-03.explanation: Cumulonimbus clouds build upward from low altitudes into towering storm clouds; cirrus, cirrostratus, and cirrocumulus are all classified as high-altitude cloud types.

2026-12-04.category: Bones of the Middle Ear, Not a Bone
2026-12-04.explanation: The cochlea is a fluid-filled, snail-shaped structure in the inner ear, not a bone; the malleus, incus, and stapes are the three tiny bones of the middle ear.

2026-12-05.explanation: Ursa Minor, Cassiopeia, and Draco are constellations made of multiple stars; Polaris is a single star, the North Star, which happens to sit at the tip of Ursa Minor.

2026-12-06.explanation: Alexander Hamilton was not a delegate in 1776 and never signed the Declaration of Independence; Jefferson, Adams, and Franklin all signed it.

2026-12-07.explanation: Arsenic is classified as a metalloid, not a halogen; fluorine, chlorine, and bromine are all halogens.

2026-12-08.category: Original 1789 US Cabinet Departments, Except a Modern Department
2026-12-08.explanation: State, Treasury, and War were three of the original US Cabinet departments established under George Washington in 1789; the Department of Homeland Security wasn't created until 2002, after the September 11 attacks.

2026-12-09.explanation: Fiji lies in the South Pacific Ocean, thousands of miles from the Caribbean; Barbados, Trinidad, and Grenada are all Caribbean islands.

2026-12-10.category: Cities in the Canadian Prairies, Except a Pacific Coast City
2026-12-10.explanation: Regina, Saskatoon, and Brandon are all cities on the Canadian Prairies; Vancouver sits on the Pacific coast of British Columbia.

2026-12-11.explanation: Hermes is the Greek messenger god; Thor, Odin, and Loki are all figures from Norse mythology.

2026-12-12.category: Capitals That Aren't the Biggest City, vs. Capital and Largest City
2026-12-12.explanation: Tokyo is both Japan's capital and its largest city; Canberra, Ottawa, and Washington D.C. are all capitals of countries whose biggest city lies elsewhere (Sydney, Toronto, and New York City, respectively).

2026-12-13.category: Greek-Rooted Shape Names, A Latin-Rooted Name
2026-12-13.explanation: "Quadrilateral" uses the Latin prefix "quadri-" for four, while heptagon, hexagon, and octagon all use Greek-rooted numerical prefixes (hepta-, hexa-, octa-).

2026-12-14.category: Alkali/Alkaline Earth Metals, Except a Transition Metal
2026-12-14.explanation: Potassium, Lithium, and Calcium are alkali or alkaline earth metals; Zinc is a transition metal in Group 12.

2026-12-15.category: Currencies Named After Units of Weight, Except One Named for a Shape
2026-12-15.explanation: The British Pound, Egyptian Pound, and Mexican Peso all derive their names from historical units of weight ("peso" is Spanish for "weight"); the Japanese Yen's name comes from a word meaning "round object," referring to the shape of coins.

2026-12-16.explanation: Hungarian belongs to the Uralic language family, related to Finnish and Estonian, not the Slavic family; Polish, Czech, and Slovak are all Slavic languages.

2026-12-17.category: Wives of Henry VIII, A 15th-Century Queen
2026-12-17.explanation: Elizabeth Woodville was queen consort to Edward IV in the 15th century, decades before Henry VIII; Catherine of Aragon, Anne Boleyn, and Jane Seymour were three of his six wives.

2026-12-18.category: SI Base Units, Not Part of the Metric System
2026-12-18.explanation: Fahrenheit is a non-metric temperature scale; the meter, kilogram, and second are all SI base units.

2026-12-19.category: Modern Fencing Weapons, A Historical Dueling Sword
2026-12-19.explanation: The rapier is a historical dueling sword, not one of the three weapons used in modern competitive fencing; foil, epee, and sabre are the actual three Olympic fencing weapons.

2026-12-20.explanation: Neptune is one of the eight full planets in our solar system; Pluto, Eris, and Ceres are all classified as dwarf planets.

2026-12-21.category: Optical Instruments, Except a Writing Machine
2026-12-21.explanation: Telescope, Microscope, and Periscope all use lenses or mirrors to view something; a Typewriter is a mechanical writing device with no optics.

2026-12-22.category: The Traditional Four Basic Tastes, Except the Modern Fifth Addition
2026-12-22.explanation: Sweet, Sour, and Salty are three of the four tastes long recognized in Western food science; Umami (savory) was only formally added as a fifth basic taste in the 20th century, based on Japanese research.

2026-12-23.category: Metals Attracted to Magnets, Not Ferromagnetic
2026-12-23.explanation: Aluminum is not attracted to ordinary magnets; iron, nickel, and cobalt are the three ferromagnetic metals at room temperature.

2026-12-24.category: Original Thirteen Colonies, Joined Later as the 14th State
2026-12-24.explanation: Vermont was an independent republic and didn't join the Union until 1791, after the original colonies; Georgia, Virginia, and Delaware were all among the original thirteen.

2026-12-25.category: Words Rooted in "Aqua", Unrelated to Water
2026-12-25.explanation: "Acquire" comes from the Latin "acquirere," meaning "to seek," and has no connection to "aqua" (water) despite the similar spelling; aquarium, aqueduct, and aquatic all genuinely derive from the water root.

2026-12-26.explanation: Chad is landlocked with no coastline; Nigeria, Ghana, and Senegal all have coastlines on the Atlantic Ocean or Gulf of Guinea.

2026-12-27.category: Countries With More Than One Official Language, Except a Monolingual-Official Country
2026-12-27.explanation: Canada (English and French), Finland (Finnish and Swedish), and Belgium (Dutch, French, and German) all have more than one official national language; Iceland recognizes only Icelandic as its official language.

2026-12-28.category: The Four Bodily Humors, Not One of the Four
2026-12-28.explanation: Ancient humor theory held that the body was governed by four humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile; bone marrow was never counted among them.

2026-12-29.category: Track and Field Throwing Events, A Jumping Event
2026-12-29.explanation: The pole vault is a jumping event, not a throw; the javelin, discus, and hammer throw are all throwing events in track and field.

2026-12-30.category: The Axial Skeleton, Part of the Limbs
2026-12-30.explanation: The femur, or thighbone, belongs to the appendicular skeleton, which makes up the limbs; the skull, ribs, and spine are all part of the axial skeleton.

2026-12-31.category: Nations Entirely South of the Equator, Straddles the Equator
2026-12-31.explanation: Indonesia's northernmost islands cross the equator into the Northern Hemisphere; Australia, New Zealand, and Madagascar lie entirely within the Southern Hemisphere.
